s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with facial and nasal swelling in a patient with recent COVID-19 infection and uncontrolled diabetes
salient_findings: Black eschar on the nasal root
Presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa
key_facts: Patient had COVID-19 infection at the end of December 2022
Patient was admitted to hospital on January 1st, 2023
Patient developed new symptoms on January 11th, including nasal ache, dyspnea, and facial and nasal swelling
Initial examination showed temperature of 36.5°C, heart rate of 116, respiratory rate of 26, blood pressure of 150/88 mmHg, and O2 saturation of 90% in room air
Laboratory tests showed white blood cell count of 2 × 10^9/L, creatinine of 178 umol/L, blood sugar of 11.6 mmol/L, and platelet count of 17 × 10^9/L
Imaging studies showed pansinusitis, bilateral lung infiltrations, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa
Blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has uncontrolled diabetes, recent COVID-19 infection, and symptoms consistent with invasive fungal infection, including facial and nasal swelling, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa

shortlist.label: Rhizopus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected Rhizopus microsporum, and patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with rhizopus infection

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms consistent with invasive fungal sinusitis, including facial and nasal swelling, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including nasal ache, dyspnea, and facial and nasal swelling, along with the presence of fungal hyphae and spores in the nasal mucosa and detection of Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus in blood mNGS, are consistent with mucormycosis, a rare but serious fungal infection that often affects immunocompromised individuals, such as those with uncontrolled diabetes.

rejected.label: Rhizopus infection
rejected.why: While Rhizopus microsporum was detected in blood mNGS, the broader diagnosis of mucormycosis encompasses infections caused by Rhizopus species and is a more comprehensive explanation of the patient's symptoms and findings.

rejected.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: While the patient has pansinusitis, the presence of fungal hyphae and spores in the nasal mucosa and detection of fungal elements in blood mNGS suggest a more systemic infection, such as mucormycosis.

rejected.label: Mucor infection
rejected.why: Mucor infection is a synonym for mucormycosis, and selecting mucormycosis as the champion provides a more specific and comprehensive diagnosis.

rejected.label: COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, including the presence of fungal hyphae and spores in the nasal mucosa and detection of Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus in blood mNGS, are not consistent with aspergillosis, which is a different type of fungal infection.

gold: Mixed mold infection with Rhizopus microsporus and Mucor racemosus causing disseminated mucormycosis
